John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island. It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s. Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt". "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight . Image caption, Burnham told campaigners in Downing Street that he would launch an independent investigation Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site. The island was a major Anglo American nuclear site in the Cold War period, lying just north of Australia. "I thought we were helping soldiers build a runway, I have no idea why, and suddenly we found out we were testing atomic bombs," Morris said. He said safety concerns when a blast went off were relaxed, with him being told to turn his back to the explosion and cover his eyes. title: Burnley MP 'appalled' by child cruelty jail term after baby dies

evidence_packet.title: Burnley MP 'appalled' by child cruelty jail term after baby dies
evidence_packet.lead: Burnley MP Oliver Ryan has called for a review of Joanna Lea's two-year sentence
evidence_packet.summary: Burnley MP Oliver Ryan has called for a review of Joanna Lea's two-year sentence
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Lancashire MP has called for a mother's two-year jail sentence to be reviewed after she admitted child cruelty offences against her three-month-old son before his death Oliver Ryan, the Labour MP for Burnley, has asked the attorney general to review the sentence handed to Joanna Lea, 36, following her conviction at Preston Crown Court on Monday Lea, from Rochdale, pleaded guilty to child cruelty offences committed before the death of her son, Allister Von Lea, in August 2022. Post-mortem examinations found cocaine and the anxiety drug pregabalin in Allister's system Ryan said he was "disgusted" by the cruelty inflicted on the baby and "appalled" by the two-year prison sentence Emergency services were called to Lea's home in Padiham at about 03:00 BST on 9 August 2022 after reports that Allister was not breathing He was pronounced dead at hospital a short time later

title: The film company in Manchester that started with £50 and a camera

evidence_packet.title: The film company in Manchester that started with £50 and a camera
evidence_packet.lead: Jacqui Carroll wanted to help other working class people gain experience in the industry
evidence_packet.summary: Jacqui Carroll wanted to help other working class people gain experience in the industry
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The film company in Manchester that started with £50 and a camera - BBC News Image caption, Jacqui Carroll wanted to give aspiring film makers new opportunities By Kelly Foran North West Published 26 November 2026 In 2001, Jacqui Carroll and Terry Egan started a film and documentary company from their home with just £50, a digital video camera and a belief that everyone has a story worth telling. Now, a quarter of a century later, the stories captured on film will form part of the North West Film Archive. REELMCR was set up to help other working class people gain opportunities and experience in an industry that Jacqui said always felt like it was for a "different class". "When I was in school I said I wanted to be an actor or an astronaut and was laughed at," she said. "I was told I could be a receptionist and that's what I ended up doing. "When I was 39 and pregnant with my daughter I had to stay in and watch TV. "That's when I realised there was nobody who sounded like me and people I knew on TV. "Even in the soaps they were putting the accents on." Image caption, Terry Egan said he felt the biggest amount of pride when the people involved watched their work Jacqui and Terry decided to set up the company in Manchester making films and documentaries as well as providing training and projects in working-class communities. From the sound engineers to the scriptwriters, everyone involved was given a chance to shine. "I was a reader and got my education in other ways," said Terry, who admits he did not attend school. "But ReelMCR... it would have been just what I needed when I was growing up. "It would have made my life easier." evidence_packet.title: Homeless charity says 'no change' in Manchester rough sleeping despite PM's pledge

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Homeless charity says 'no change' in Manchester rough sleeping despite PM's pledge - BBC News Image caption, Dave Evans co-founded a homeless charity to help support those in need By Anna Jameson and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 26 November 2026 A homeless charity's co-founder has said he fears Andy Burnham will not be able to meet his pledge to end rough sleeping as the number of those sleeping on the streets in Manchester continues to rise. When he entered Downing Street in the summer, the prime minister pledged to provide a route out of rough sleeping by Christmas through a £442m package of emergency accommodation and practical support over three years. A further £432m was added to the scheme in October. However, with just weeks to go until Christmas, Dave Evans, from the Two Brews charity, said he believed rough sleeping had "gone up dramatically" as he witnessed the daily struggle of those on the streets. When Burnham was first elected as the Mayor of Greater Manchester in May 2017, he made the same pledge to end the need for rough sleeping across all 10 boroughs. He made a great start with the number of rough sleepers in Greater Manchester reducing during the pandemic to 89 in 2021 from 268 in 2017. But over the last five years, numbers have been creeping up. The latest annual rough sleeping snapshot, where local authorities in England provide a figure on any one night in Autumn, shows Greater Manchester has 197 rough sleepers, 43 more than in 2024. The figures for 2026 are expected early next year. 'Big increase' Jordan Parker, from Two Brews, said he and Evans had started the charity six years ago. title: Gender-critical equality officer unfairly sacked by council

evidence_packet.title: Gender-critical equality officer unfairly sacked by council
evidence_packet.lead: Lorna Young was subjected to a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her social media posts, a judge rules
evidence_packet.summary: Lorna Young was subjected to a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her social media posts, a judge rules
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An equality and diversity manager was unfairly sacked after a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her liking or commenting on posts critical of transgender ideology, a judge has ruled Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , external , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable

evidence_packet.summary: A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment" John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nu
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment" John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt" "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A homeless charity's co-founder has said he fears Andy Burnham will not be able to meet his pledge to end rough sleeping as the number of those sleeping on the streets in Manchester continues to rise When he entered Downing Street in the summer, the prime minister pledged to provide a route out of rough sleeping by Christmas through a £442m package of emergency accommodation and practical support over three years A further £432m was added to the scheme in October However, with just weeks to go until Christmas, Dave Evans, from the Two Brews charity, said he believed rough sleeping had "gone up dramatically" as he witnessed the daily struggle of those on the streets When Burnham was first elected as the Mayor of Greater Manchester in May 2017, he made the same pledge to end the need for rough sleeping across all 10 boroughs He made a great start with the number of rough sleepers in Greater Manchester reducing during the pandemic to 89 in 2021 from 268 in 2017

evidence_packet.title: Gender-critical equality officer unfairly sacked by council

evidence_packet.summary: An equality and diversity manager was unfairly sacked after a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her liking or commenting on posts critical of transgender ideology, a judge has ruled Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account o
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An equality and diversity manager was unfairly sacked after a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her liking or commenting on posts critical of transgender ideology, a judge has ruled Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , external , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable

As he made his way into the witness box, where his wife had calmly answered questions for 45 minut Why, after initially pleading not guilty, then changing his plea, was this the moment he wanted to speak out? “So the court knows the truth of what happened to my wife, so my wife knows and I’m here to tell the truth and give my account of what actually happened," he said In a navy suit and tie, the husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, faced questioning from prosecutors all day on Thursday (November 26). A consultation on the city-region’s first Bus Network Accessibility Plan starts next week which hopes to get a wide range of feedback how bus travel can be improved The draft plan states that several barriers to accessibility remain on the network These include access to bus stops, availability of passenger information, ease of boarding, availability of assistance and the consistency of facilities at Greater Manchester’s interchanges Recent changes to improve accessibility have included audio-visual announcements and next-stop screens on buses, hearing loops, high-contrast handrails and anti-slip flooring Newer buses also include two dedicated wheelchair spaces and room for an assistance dog close to its owner

Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter A Salford councillor is giving locals a ‘gift’ in the run up to Christmas . Residents in Eccles will benefit from free parking at the area’s seven car parks on the three Saturdays leading up to the festive period The move will save residents a ‘small amount of money in the run up to the most expensive time of year’, according to local councillor Mike McCusker. The scheme applies to seven council-run car parks in Eccles, Monton, and Swinton , which are on Hankinson Way, John William Street The scheme is also geared at supporting local businesses, with the hope that locals might make use of their highstreet offers instead of ordering all their Christmas shopping online Councillor McCusker, who represents Eccles, said: “We’ve got a gift for you in the seven car parks that Salford City Council runs. You can get free parking on the free Saturdays leading up to Christmas. It will help you save a small amount of money at this expensive time of year. He added: “We’re delighted to bring back free festive parking this Christmas, helping residents save a little extra money at what can be an expensive time of year, while giving our local businesses a welcome boost

Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group worked with Canadian officials to pull off the dramatic bust on Wednesday evening (November 25) Greater Manchester Police says it was alerted about plans to smuggle 590kg of cannabis by Canadian authorities. It was concealed among a large shipment headed to the UK According to police, drug dealers had created sophisticated compartments inside a container with the hopes that the illegal drugs would go undetected. Then, the prosecutor laid out charge after charge which he has admitted, 60 crimes committed over a 20 year period until his arrest in October last year. A consultation on the city-region’s first Bus Network Accessibility Plan starts next week which hopes to get a wide range of feedback how bus travel can be improved The draft plan states that several barriers to accessibility remain on the network These include access to bus stops, availability of passenger information, ease of boarding, availability of assistance and the consistency of facilities at Greater Manchester’s interchanges Recent changes to improve accessibility have included audio-visual announcements and next-stop screens on buses, hearing loops, high-contrast handrails and anti-slip flooring Newer buses also include two dedicated wheelchair spaces and room for an assistance dog close to its owner

I can be my version of me, not his' Selena is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who secured a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) in the last two y ‘It got me home’, Selena tells me. She is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who have had a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) issued over the last two years Hers is the result of an abusive relationship she says started when she was 16. The court-issued order puts legally binding restrictions on her now ex-boyfriend, including blocking him from contacting her or entering anywhere he believes she could be The 23-year-old, who we are calling Selena, said the relationship had turned her into ‘his version’ of her. She credits the DAPO as a huge part of the reason she was able to reclaim her life and her home for herself and her young daughter Selena said her ex breached her DAPO twice. He pleaded guilty and is currently awaiting sentencing for that second breach She told the Manchester Evening News the relationship started in 2019 when she was 16, ‘very young’, ‘naïve’ and ‘impressionable’. The northbound section of Alan Turing Way, in Beswick close to the Etihad Stadium , was shut off in March after a suspected sinkhole was discovered For months the council wasn’t entirely sure what had caused the stretch of road to collapse. But in September, engineers discovered it was a 50m-deep mineshaft under the road that triggered the 3m-wide crater There is a long history of mining and colliers throughout east Manchester, but this mineshaft wasn’t recorded on historic maps and took workers by surprise. Further investigations revealed the extent of the cavity and scale of repairs required In order to stabilise the shaft, contractors filled it with 120 tonnes of concrete grout before putting a ‘reinforced concrete slab’ over the top. Concrete has also been used to 'backfill' the original excavation with utilities pipes, and the road surface, then being restored In an update, Manchester City Council said the 'unprecedented' and 'highly complex' works were 'reaching their conclusion' and that the road would reopen on Saturday, November 28. Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group worked with Canadian officials to pull off the dramatic bust on Wednesday evening (November 25) Greater Manchester Police says it was alerted about plans to smuggle 590kg of cannabis by Canadian authorities. It was concealed among a large shipment headed to the UK According to police, drug dealers had created sophisticated compartments inside a container with the hopes that the illegal drugs would go undetected. The container, which arrived at the docks in Liverpool, was closely followed as it was delivered by an HGV to an address in Heywo Officers covertly watched as several people interacted with the container, a spokesperson for GMP said. A consultation on the city-region’s first Bus Network Accessibility Plan starts next week which hopes to get a wide range of feedback how bus travel can be improved The draft plan states that several barriers to accessibility remain on the network These include access to bus stops, availability of passenger information, ease of boarding, availability of assistance and the consistency of facilities at Greater Manchester’s interchanges Recent changes to improve accessibility have included audio-visual announcements and next-stop screens on buses, hearing loops, high-contrast handrails and anti-slip flooring Newer buses also include two dedicated wheelchair spaces and room for an assistance dog close to its owner

She is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who have had a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) issued over the last two years Hers is the result of an abusive relationship she says started when she was 16. The northbound section of Alan Turing Way, in Beswick close to the Etihad Stadium , was shut off in March after a suspected sinkhole was discovered For months the council wasn’t entirely sure what had caused the stretch of road to collapse. But in September, engineers discovered it was a 50m-deep mineshaft under the road that triggered the 3m-wide crater There is a long history of mining and colliers throughout east Manchester, but this mineshaft wasn’t recorded on historic maps and took workers by surprise. Further investigations revealed the extent of the cavity and scale of repairs required In order to stabilise the shaft, contractors filled it with 120 tonnes of concrete grout before putting a ‘reinforced concrete slab’ over the top. Concrete has also been used to 'backfill' the original excavation with utilities pipes, and the road surface, then being restored In an update, Manchester City Council said the 'unprecedented' and 'highly complex' works were 'reaching their conclusion' and that the road would reopen on Saturday, November 28. It is expected to be clear by mid-morning

title: Nuclear veteran says investigation a 'magical moment'

evidence_packet.title: Nuclear veteran says investigation a 'magical moment'
evidence_packet.lead: John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation i
evidence_packet.summary: John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation i
evidence_packet.evidence_text: John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt" "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site The island was a major Anglo American nuclear site in the Cold War period, lying just north of Australia

title: Gender-critical equality officer unfairly sacked by council

evidence_packet.title: Gender-critical equality officer unfairly sacked by council
evidence_packet.lead: Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devo
evidence_packet.summary: Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable The judge said Young suffered from a disability affecting her sight, but also became physically and mentally very ill during the lengthy investigation, and at one point made an attempt on her own life

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he's done this?", a court heard The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's right to anonymity, has admitted a litany of offences against her - including rape, administering a substance with intent and inviting 13 other men to join the abuse Nine of those men have pleaded not guilty to sexual offences against her and are standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Giving evidence in court for the first time, the woman also said claims she had been "pretending to be asleep" during the abuse were a "load of rubbish" The victim, in her 60s, was formally interviewed by Greater Manchester Police on 7 November last year, around two weeks after officers had arrived at her family home to arrest her husband In the interview, played to the jury, she told Det Con Anouska Barker: "I had no knowledge of what you told me had happened and I still can't believe it's true, and I think you have made a mistake."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

In August, Nothing Gold Can Stay took Robert Frost’s poem about transience as its starting point. Where that show dwelt on things passing, this one is more interested in what lasts The four contributing artists each approach time differently, thinking about how the past and the future shape the way ideas are understood. Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. Olivia England, who graduated from Manchester School of Art alongside Clough, reworks found objects, text and imagery through bookbinding and print, while London-based Elliot Fo Seeing the work from a perspective that isn’t your own is meant to open up conversations about the legacy of ideas, collective memory and what our actions leave behind for people we’ll never meet

title: Man City charges meeting interrupted as Premier League send 'furious messages'

evidence_packet.title: Man City charges meeting interrupted as Premier League send 'furious messages'
evidence_packet.lead: The Premier League interrupted a Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee meeting in Westminster where the Manchester City case was discussed
evidence_packet.summary: The Premier League interrupted a Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee meeting in Westminster where the Manchester City case was discussed
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Man City charges meeting interrupted as Premier League send 'furious messages' The Premier League interrupted a Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee meeting in Westminster where the Manchester City case was discussed Add to preferred sourc Premier League bosses interrupted a Commons select committee hearing to deny claims they have spent £500million in legal fees on the Manchester City case. The charges had been discussed as MPs questioned Independent Football Regulator (IFR) chair David Kogan and chief executive R City were charged in February 2023 with 115 alleged breaches of financial rules spanning nine seasons between 2009 and 2018, with the club accused of inflating sponsorship deals and concealing payments to players and managers Following a private hearing in late 2024, an independent commission published its verdict on September 29, finding City guilty on 114 of the 115 charges . It was ruled the club used "sham" contracts to inflate revenues by more than £900m. City have strenuously denied all wrongdoi The Premier League's legal costs incurred in this case were quoted at a meeting on Wednesday by Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage as being in the region of £500m. После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он приобрел большую и преданную аудиторию как в Турции, так и за ее пределами. 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов. Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне! Предварительный заказ
